headline: Non-cash derivative losses swing results to a loss
summary_short: Cheniere's revenue rose 7.8% y/y to $5,868.0 million on higher Henry Hub-linked LNG pricing and volumes, but $4.8 billion of unfavorable fair-value changes on long-term IPM supply derivatives swung net income to a $3,502.0 million loss (EPS -$16.65).
summary_long: Cheniere's loss was non-cash: net income fell $3.9 billion y/y to -$3,502 million as $4.8 billion of unfavorable fair-value swings on long-term IPM supply derivatives -- tied to widening global-vs-domestic gas spreads and Middle East volatility -- swamped otherwise favorable results. Revenue rose $424 million to $5,868 million on higher Henry Hub pricing and 66 TBtu more volume, mostly from added Corpus Christi Stage 3 trains. Operating cash flow held at $1,080 million (vs $1,228 million a year ago). Cheniere repurchased $537 million of stock, paid a $0.555/share dividend, and expanded its buyback authorization to $10 billion. Long-term debt eased to $22,143 million; equity fell to $3,755 million on the quarter's loss. No forward guidance was disclosed.

drivers.explanation: A $1.3B increase from higher Henry Hub-linked LNG pricing and volumes delivered (+66 TBtu) was partly offset by $952M of unfavorable derivative fair-value changes included in revenue.
Cost of sales rose $4.9B, mostly $4.2B of unfavorable fair-value swings on long-term IPM derivative agreements plus higher feedstock gas costs, partly offset by a $370M tax-credit reduction.

Net income fell $3.9B y/y as $4.8B of unfavorable derivative fair-value changes (mostly long-term IPM agreements) swamped higher revenue, partly offset by a $462M lower tax provision and smaller NCI allocation.
The per-share swing mirrors the net-income decline; diluted weighted-average shares also fell about 6% y/y on continued buybacks, modestly widening the per-share loss.

The entire swing to a loss is non-cash mark-to-market on long-term gas-price derivatives amid widening global-vs-domestic spreads and Middle East-driven volatility; operating cash flow held up and buybacks/dividend continued.
